newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas soybean, cotton harvest under way.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas soybean, cotton harvest under way.

text.p: Harvesting of cotton and soybeans began in Arkansas during the week ended Sunday, while corn, rice and sorghum harvesting advanced, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.

Cotton was one percent harvested versus none a year ago and on average. Sixty-four percent had open bolls versus 62 a year ago and the 37 average. The crop was rated 19 percent excellent, 48 good, 28 fair and five poor.

Soybeans were four percent harvested versus none a year ago and on average. Nine percent was mature versus none a year ago and the one percent average. The crop was rated 14 percent excellent, 38 good, 31 fair, 13 poor and four very poor.
Several counties reported treating soybeans for insect pests such as bollworms and podworms.
Corn harvest was 58 percent complete versus 75 a year ago and the 62 average. The crop was rated 26 excellent, 44 good, 20 fair, seven poor and three very poor.
Sorghum was 39 percent harvested against 32 a year ago and the 35 average. The crop was rated nine percent excellent, 46 good, 34 fair, and 11 poor.
Rice was 15 percent harvested versus 15 a year ago and the 16 average. The crop was rated 26 percent excellent, 54 good, 18 fair and two poor.
Soil moisture was rated three percent surplus, 49 adequate, 36 short and 12 very short.
